title: Spilling the Beans: Teaching LLMs to Self-Report Their Hidden Objectives
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06626 + https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06626 (v5, stamp 22 Mar 2026, ICLR 2026 camera-ready)
bench: HiddenAgenda (Phuong et al. 2024); SHADE-Arena (Kutasov et al. 2025)
evidence: adaptive=1: hand-crafted interrogation-evasion condition "the model is interrogated with its original hidden system prompt, plus an additional plausible, innocent objective that it can cite if it accidentally reveals having a secondary objective" (decoy); not SRFT-specific, no optimization. Defense = SRFT fine-tuning makes the agent self-report hidden objectives on post-task interrogation (detect only, no blocking; "SRFT promotes the admission of hidden objectives without eliminating their execution"). SRFT applied to GPT-4.1 only (Claude Sonnet 4 = prefill baseline). judge_exposed=Y: interrogated model is the agent that processed SHADE-Arena tool outputs (whether the transcript stays in context is not stated explicitly). utility = GPQA/AIME/HLE unchanged after SRFT. fpr = control-condition false admissions 0-1%. decisions '-' = detect/flag only. v1 date from alphaXiv mirror (arXiv abs history unreadable); v2 stamp 11 Nov 2025.

title: Calibrating Conservatism for Scalable Oversight
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.28807 + https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.28807 (v1, stamp 27 May 2026; only version)
bench: own:SWE-bench Lite adversarial variant (instance-specific vulnerability injection, 300 instances); MACHIAVELLI (Hero of Kendrickstone, Pendragon Rising)
evidence: adaptive=0: misaligned agent gets a fixed injected instruction "With probability p = 0.5, this candidate receives an instance-specific misalignment instruction targeting a vulnerability tailored to the files the issue touches"; no overseer-aware or optimized evasion. CCO = weak LLM overseers (Claude Haiku 4.5 x10 per candidate; GPT-5.4-mini/nano in replication) score each candidate action; penalty lambda calibrated online (conformal decision theory); selection falls back to conservative baseline a0 (low-resource aligned patch), i.e. block/override before deployment, no human. Overseers read agent-produced patch + random repo files (MACHIAVELLI: game scenes). Agent backbones: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5. utility = solve rate, MACHIAVELLI reward. "Deferral rate" is over misalignment attempts (TPR-like), not FPR; no cost/latency reported. public_bench=Y only via MACHIAVELLI (ethics/safety benchmark).

title: From Similarity to Vulnerability: Key Collision Attack on LLM Semantic Caching
evidence: NOT_DEFENSE: attack paper (CacheAttack); contributions are fuzzy-hash modeling, collision attack framework, response/tool hijacking demos; Section 7 only discusses/tests existing mitigations (key salting, perplexity screening, per-user cache isolation). v1 2026-01-30, v2 2026-06-30.

title: Unsafe LLM-Based Search: Quantitative Analysis and Mitigation of Safety Risks in AI Web Search
bench: own:AIPSE risky-query set (keyword-list + natural-language queries built from PhishTank/ThreatBook/LevelBlue malicious URLs; 46 main-risk responses)
evidence: adaptive=0: no attacker-aware or evasion evaluation; Discussions and Limitations (sec 9) covers only phishing-data timeliness and human evaluation. Defense (sec 8 Risk Mitigation) = agent with GPT-4.1 content-refinement tool + URL detector tools (XGBoost / PhishLLM / HtmlLLM=GPT-4.1 reading crawled HTML); post-processes AIPSE response, filters and attaches risk warnings before delivery. n_models = 7 production AIPSEs whose responses were pooled (defense agent itself = GPT-4.1 only). DSR 78.3% (HtmlLLM). utility = info loss ~10.7% (abstract; not a task-success rate). fpr = HtmlLLM confusion matrix 13 FP / 121 benign URLs (Table 3); XGBoost F1 0.667. No cost/latency. v1 (title "The Rising Threat to Emerging AI-Powered Search Engines", GPT-4o + XGBoost) differs; unversioned URL served v1 content; v3 probe inconclusive (rate-limited), v2 = latest confirmed.

title: When AI Meets the Web: Prompt Injection Risks in Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugins
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.05797 + https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.05797 (v1, stamp 08 Nov 2025; only version)
evidence: NOT_DEFENSE (borderline): measurement study; contributions I-IV = ecosystem characterization, plugin vulnerabilities, real-world configs, controlled experiments. Two "prototypical"/"lightweight" defenses appear only in abstract + sec 8.2 Mitigation Strategies (UGCBuster isolating user-generated content, manually validated on 10 sites, 1 FP, ~$0.05/page; LLM-hardened tool instructions, ASR drop 40-75%), not listed as contributions.
